statement: World Bank analysis reports rapid observed warming since the 1980s and projects substantially higher end-century temperatures under RCP8.5 than RCP4.5.
compact_statement: Observed and projected warming raises Ukraine's heat baseline.

source_refs.locator: pp. 15 and 31, executive summary climate paragraph and Table 1

uncertainty: The physical signal is clear, but model spread, future emissions, and war-altered land systems remain uncertain.

statement: Official assessments identify heat, drought, river and urban flooding, wildfire, and divergent seasonal water balance, with greater drying risk in parts of southern and central Ukraine.
compact_statement: Heat, drought, flood, wildfire, and seasonal pressures vary geographically.

source_refs.locator: pp. 3 and 16, executive summary and precipitation and hazard paragraphs
pp. 16-17, executive summary regional and seasonal projections

uncertainty: Temperature direction is clearer than local precipitation magnitude, and not every observed event is climate-attributable.

statement: World Bank modelling projects large expansion of rainfed cropland exposed to green-water scarcity at 1.5 and 3 degrees Celsius warming, especially in east-central areas.
compact_statement: Warming can substantially expand rainfed-cropland water exposure.

source_refs.locator: p. 16, Box 3, green-water-scarcity estimates

uncertainty: The modelling was described as forthcoming and is neither observed nor fully war-adjusted.

statement: Ukraine's adaptation communication identifies data gaps, limited capacity at all administrative levels, reactive planning, weak monitoring, and insufficient cost-benefit evidence as adaptation barriers.
compact_statement: Data, staffing, coordination, appraisal, and monitoring constrain adaptation delivery.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 31-33 (printed pp. 26-28), section 3.3 and "Means of Adaptation Implementation and Support Needs"

uncertainty: Official self-assessment does not quantify current capacity in each jurisdiction.

statement: RDNA5 estimates national-scale war damage, losses, and recovery needs across housing, transport, energy, agriculture, water, municipal services, and ecosystems through December 2025.
compact_statement: War destruction has altered the systems and assets underlying climate exposure and recovery.

source_refs.locator: pp. 6-7, definitions and overview table

uncertainty: War damage is not climate impact; inaccessible territories and evolving methods limit completeness, and needs are not committed finance.

statement: RDNA5 reports extensive irrigation damage and a sharp production decline on formerly irrigated land affected by loss of irrigation service, concentrated in southern and eastern systems.
compact_statement: War-related irrigation loss sharply reduced production in affected systems.

source_refs.locator: p. 35 (report p. 33), Irrigation and Water Resources chapter

uncertainty: Conflict damage is the principal cause of reported loss; future climate scarcity is only a potential compounding pressure.

statement: OHCHR documents attacks on energy infrastructure coinciding with severe winter cold and disrupting electricity, heating, water, health services, and schooling in government-controlled areas.
compact_statement: Attacks converted severe cold exposure into multisystem service failure.

source_refs.locator: p. 5 (report p. 1) and pp. 11-12 (report pp. 7-8), energy and household service impacts

uncertainty: The compounded weather-war effect is documented; the cold spell is not attributed to anthropogenic climate change.

statement: Backup generators, water distribution, and Points of Invincibility provided emergency coping during outages, but mobility limits and dependence on lifts or pumped water left unequal access.
compact_statement: Emergency coping reduced but did not equalize outage impacts.

source_refs.locator: pp. 11-12 (report pp. 7-8), household and service-impact sections

uncertainty: Availability is documented, not population-wide use or counterfactual effectiveness.

statement: Early-war research identified widespread realized or potential impacts on water resources and infrastructure, including complete water-system failure in multiple settlements.
compact_statement: Hostilities rapidly disrupted water systems and reduced coping capacity.

source_refs.locator: Results section, 'Impacts on water resources and infrastructure' and geographic-results paragraphs

uncertainty: An early and incomplete incident inventory likely undercounts inaccessible areas and does not quantify climate attribution.

statement: The Kakhovka dam breach caused downstream inundation and upstream reservoir desiccation affecting settlements, wetlands, forests, agriculture, water supply, and irrigation.
compact_statement: Kakhovka caused simultaneous inundation and desiccation as a conflict-related infrastructure disaster.
ecological_level: reservoir, floodplain, wetlands, and irrigation systems

source_refs.locator: p. 10 (report p. ix) and p. 88 (report p. 74), impact summary and long-term effects

uncertainty: The breach and broad impacts are established, but it is not a climate flood and inaccessible-area and long-term ecological evidence remain incomplete.

statement: RDNA5 and JRC document mines and unexploded ordnance, industrial contamination, burned landscapes, soil degradation, forest loss and ecosystem damage in conflict-affected areas; these harms plausibly constrain safe land access and ecological and productive functions relevant to future adaptation.
compact_statement: Conflict-related environmental degradation may erode foundations of climate resilience.

source_refs.locator: p. 44 (report p. 42), Environment chapter
PDF pp. 42-50, chapters 5-6 on forest cover/fire and soil degradation/contamination

uncertainty: Component harms are observed, but their complete effect on future adaptation outcomes is not evaluated.

statement: Hotter and drier fire weather can raise background wildfire risk while warfare adds ignition, explosive contamination, and restrictions on monitoring and suppression.
compact_statement: Climate fire weather and conflict constraints can compound wildfire risk.

source_refs.locator: pp. 37-44, forest-fire spatial analysis and climate-risk sections
pp. 2-8 and 16, climate-environment-conflict framing and causal cautions

uncertainty: Component mechanisms are supported, but spatial overlap does not attribute individual fires to climate or warfare.

statement: War displacement has redistributed population, service demand, housing needs, and municipal revenue, while pre-war staffing capacity already varied between urban, settlement, and rural municipalities.
compact_statement: Displacement and uneven municipal capacity create differentiated local vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: pp. 14-15 and 66-67, displacement and service-demand evidence
p. 285 (report p. 283), municipal staffing survey
pp. 1-3, IDP strategy targets, responsibilities, and implementation timing

uncertainty: Displacement is dynamic, occupied-area data are incomplete, and the staffing baseline predates the full-scale war.

statement: The Mykolaiv Recovered evaluation found local service, coordination, and project-management gains alongside reduced green ambition, inconsistent inclusion, administrative burdens, and limited follow-up.
compact_statement: Independent evaluation found recovery gains and environmental, inclusion, and transaction-cost trade-offs.

source_refs.locator: pp. 3-6 and 10, executive findings, conclusions, and recommendations

uncertainty: Credible local evaluation without a counterfactual; findings are not nationally representative or climate-impact estimates.

statement: The Mykolaiv evaluation documents locally anchored recovery offices, coordination, community initiatives, and institutional capacity that can support inclusive recovery, while sustainability depends on local staffing and finance.
compact_statement: Area-based recovery created selected local resilience and coordination capacity.

source_refs.locator: pp. 3 and 6, executive summary and conclusions on services, recovery offices, capacity, and sustainability

uncertainty: The local qualitative evaluation cannot establish causal climate-resilience or peace outcomes.

statement: JRC records substantial municipal climate-planning participation, while UNEP recommends that Kakhovka reconstruction alternatives use monitoring, nature-based options, and future climate and water projections rather than automatic restoration of the prior design.
compact_statement: Municipal planning participation and climate-informed reconstruction recommendations indicate potential adaptive capacity, not implementation outcomes.

source_refs.locator: p. 6 and local-governance section, Covenant of Mayors participation and plan counts
p. 85 (report p. 71), reconstruction recommendations

uncertainty: Participation counts and recommendations show formal or intended capacity, not consistent implementation or outcomes.

statement: Source dated 2024-10-02 reports: Military operations destroyed Mykolaiv’s Dnipro intake on 12 April 2022, cutting drinking water to the city’s roughly 470,000 residents.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-10-02 reports: Military operations destroyed Mykolaiv’s Dnipro intake on 12 April 2022, cutting drinking water to the city’s roughly 470,000 residents.

source_refs.locator: Section 1, paragraph describing the April 2022 damage to the Dnipro–Mykolaiv pipeline.

uncertainty: A conflict-related service loss, not climate-attributed.

statement: Source dated 2024-10-02 reports: By 2024, remote-area wells yielded 5,000–10,000 m³/day against pre-war demand of at least 80,000; reported quality exceeded drinking-water limits and water was trucked daily.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-10-02 reports: By 2024, remote-area wells yielded 5,000–10,000 m³/day against pre-war demand of at least 80,000; reported quality exceeded drinking-water limits and water was trucked daily.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.1, paragraphs on alternative wells and water delivery to remote parts of Mykolaiv.

uncertainty: Study-period conditions, not October 2026 status.

statement: For Mykolaiv's proposed Southern Bug alternative, the study models water-supply plus minimum environmental-flow requirements reaching 40–79% of flow in May–October 2051–2080 under SSP5-8.5.
compact_statement: For Mykolaiv's proposed Southern Bug alternative, the study models water-supply plus minimum environmental-flow requirements reaching 40–79% of flow in May–October 2051–2080 under SSP5-8.5.
scenario: SSP5-8.5; far-future 2051–2080, as specified by the authors.

source_refs.locator: Sections 2.3.1–2.3.2 and 3, modeled flow results for the proposed Southern Bug supply.

uncertainty: The share includes environmental-flow requirements as well as municipal supply, not city withdrawals alone or a present shortage.

statement: Source dated 2026-04-25 reports: The study says the 2023 Kakhovka destruction increased the Dnipro–Donbas canal’s importance as a water and food-security route for Ukraine’s steppe zone.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-04-25 reports: The study says the 2023 Kakhovka destruction increased the Dnipro–Donbas canal’s importance as a water and food-security route for Ukraine’s steppe zone.

source_refs.locator: Abstract and section 2.1, study-area description after the 2023 Kakhovka destruction.

uncertainty: The source describes a changed post-destruction role; it does not quantify local household water losses.

statement: Source dated 2026-04-25 reports: From 2015–2024, up to one-quarter of sampled canal water during low-flow periods was classed as only limited-suitability irrigation water; the authors attribute salinity changes to low flows, evaporation and combined climate and infrastructure pressures.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-04-25 reports: From 2015–2024, up to one-quarter of sampled canal water during low-flow periods was classed as only limited-suitability irrigation water; the authors attribute salinity changes to low flows, evaporation and combined climate and infrastructure pressures.
institutions: Regional Water Resources Office in Dnipropetrovsk Region

source_refs.locator: Abstract and section 5, conclusions on monitoring results and combined pressures.

uncertainty: Sparse seasonal monitoring; combined low-flow/evaporation and infrastructure pressures are not separately identified. Not an attribution of every 2015–2024 water-quality change to war or climate.

statement: Source dated 2026-04-22 reports: UNDP reports 30 municipal ESCO solar contracts across 22 cities, totalling 5.1 MW and intended to serve 541,000 people; it says these installations eased pressure on damaged grids and helped maintain services during attacks and outages.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-04-22 reports: UNDP reports 30 municipal ESCO solar contracts across 22 cities, totalling 5.1 MW and intended to serve 541,000 people; it says these installations eased pressure on damaged grids and helped maintain services during attacks and outages.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 12, energy-services results and municipal solar contracts.

uncertainty: Thirty contracts/5.1 MW and intended population reach are reported; contract signing is not confirmation that every installation was commissioned or service maintained at every site.

statement: Source dated 2026-04-22 reports: UNDP reports energy equipment support that restored or maintained services for more than 6.6 million people; it also says attacks delayed commissioning of several units.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-04-22 reports: UNDP reports energy equipment support that restored or maintained services for more than 6.6 million people; it also says attacks delayed commissioning of several units.
affected_groups: people reliant on supported energy services

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 12, energy recovery results paragraph.

uncertainty: National energy-recovery outputs and commissioning delays under attacks; not a measured climate-adaptation outcome or local causal estimate.

statement: Source dated 2026-01-04 reports: The ministry reported that more than 570 MW of new public-sector distributed-generation capacity had been commissioned by January 2026; it says modular boilers and co-generation can operate near users when large facilities are damaged or de-energized.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-01-04 reports: The ministry reported that more than 570 MW of new public-sector distributed-generation capacity had been commissioned by January 2026; it says modular boilers and co-generation can operate near users when large facilities are damaged or de-energized.
institutions: Ministry for Communities and Territories Development

source_refs.locator: Paragraphs on distributed generation commissioned and municipal heat/water operation.

uncertainty: The capacity total is national; the article does not provide named local allocations or independently measured continuity outcomes.

statement: Source dated 2026-01-04 reports: The ministry says UAH 665 million was allocated in 2025 to frontline oblasts for fuel supporting municipal and critical-infrastructure operation.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-01-04 reports: The ministry says UAH 665 million was allocated in 2025 to frontline oblasts for fuel supporting municipal and critical-infrastructure operation.
institutions: Ministry for Communities and Territories Development

source_refs.locator: Paragraph on 2025 support for frontline oblasts.

uncertainty: The release does not identify recipient oblasts or report service outcomes attributable to the fuel support.
